title: Justification
definition: Justification is God's act of declaring a sinner righteous through faith in Jesus Christ apart from works.
summary: Justification means believers are accepted by God because of Christ's righteousness rather than their own.
christFocus: Jesus accomplished justification through His death and resurrection, providing the righteousness believers receive through faith.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Justification is a legal declaration from God. In justification, God does not pretend sinners are righteous in themselves. He declares those who trust in Christ righteous because of Christ's finished work and righteousness.

This doctrine is received by faith, not earned by works. Human effort cannot erase guilt or produce the righteousness God requires. Christ obeyed, died, and rose so believers could be counted righteous in Him.

Justification brings peace with God. The believer no longer stands condemned but accepted in Christ, secure in the righteousness of another.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people carry guilt because they believe they must earn God's acceptance or make up for their past. Justification matters because it gives assurance that acceptance with God rests on Christ's finished work, not personal performance.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Rest your confidence before God in Christ alone. When accused by guilt or pride, return to the truth that righteousness is received by faith. Live gratefully, not anxiously, because you are accepted in Christ.
